subject: Re: Throughput & SLO follow-up — FinEx workload details
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@finex.com>
Date: 2026-02-27T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: throughput & latency targets from today's call

Hi Marissa — thanks again for the call this morning. Carlos and I talked through the high level and wanted to capture a few concrete numbers so we can model cost and capacity on our side. Can you confirm the following items from Redwood's perspective: 1) typical end-to-end latency SLO you recommend for streaming chat scenarios; 2) practical sustained tokens/sec and peak tokens/sec per dedicated instance for the recommended model family; and 3) how concurrent sessions map to GPU concurrency (we have sessions that stay open for streaming).

A bit about our workload: primary flow is low-latency chat for financial agents (single-turn and multi-turn), roughly 10K active users during US business hours with 600 concurrent streaming sessions at peak. Average response length is ~120 tokens, but some assistant tasks produce up to 1,200 tokens. We also have batch reranking jobs overnight that will run ~5k requests of 50 candidates.

Can you also attach whatever sizing calc you used on the call? That will help our infra team. Thanks — Samantha

Best,
Samantha
Head of Engineering, FinEx Inc
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & latency targets from today's call

Hi Samantha — great to chat. Attaching the sizing calc and a short recap (attached: redwood-sizing-calculator.xlsx). Quick answers up front, then a few clarifying questions so our sizing matches your production profile: 

Summary answers (ballpark for recommended M-family variant):
- Recommended latency SLO (streaming chat): 95th percentile end-to-end token latency <= 120ms for live agent UX. If you need sub-100ms we can discuss higher tier or placement in dedicated pools.
- Sustained tokens/sec per instance (steady-state): ~25k tokens/sec for the M-family quantized to int8 on T4-class instance profiles; for higher-capacity A100/80GB variants expect ~75k sustained tokens/sec.
- Peak tokens/sec (burst): up to ~150k tokens/sec on autoscale with burst capacity enabled (depends on model size and KV cache hit rates).
- Concurrency mapping: In streaming cases we typically provision based on concurrent streams where each stream consumes a small steady per-session CPU/GPU schedule (KV cache plus small incremental decoding). Example: on M-family T4 profiles we expect ~150-250 concurrent low-latency streams per instance (varies with model, sequence length).

Clarifying questions to finalize the sizing:
1) Of the 600 concurrent streaming sessions you mentioned, what fraction are actively generating tokens at any given second vs idle/open? (e.g., 20% actively generating results)
2) For multi-turn sessions, what's the typical average prefix length (tokens retained in KV cache) we should assume? This affects memory and cache-hit sizing.
3) For the 1,200-token responses, are those tail-heavy but infrequent (e.g., 1-2% of requests) or more common?
4) For reranking batch jobs, are the 5k requests spread evenly overnight or burst within a 30-60 minute window?

Next steps I propose: Rafael will take the sizing calc and produce two capacity plans (steady-state + peak) and an option with Dedicated pool sizing + estimated monthly cost. If you can reply with the clarifications above, we'll drop a follow-up with concrete instance counts and recommended routing policies (e.g., separate Dedicated pool for streaming vs batch rerank).

Also attaching a mutual action plan template for procurement (mutual-action-plan.docx) — ping me if you'd like a DocuSign link instead.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@finex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & latency targets from today's call

Marissa/Rafael — quick answers from our infra team below so you can proceed with the capacity plan: 

- Active generating fraction: ~35% of concurrent sessions are actively generating tokens at a given second (most sessions are interactive; about 65% are idle but connected for streaming).
- Average prefix length in KV cache: 220 tokens per active session (multi-turn history and system prompt combined). We expect session length to grow over time but will trim at 1,000 tokens as a retention policy.
- Long responses: ~3% of responses exceed 1,000 tokens; typical tail is 1,200-1,500 tokens.
- Reranking batch pattern: 5k requests run in a 2-hour window overnight (spikey but off-peak).

Also, one ask on SLAs: we need p50 latency for interactive flows around 50-70ms and p95 <= 120ms. If Redwood can guarantee p95 <= 120ms in a Dedicated pool with 99.9% uptime, that helps our procurement team.

Thanks,
Carlos
VP Product, FinEx Inc
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finex.com>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & latency targets from today's call

Thanks Carlos — that's very helpful. Rafael and I ran the numbers and here's the proposed sizing + next steps (attached detailed calc):

Proposed capacity (M-family / mixed instance plan):
- Steady-state: 6 dedicated T4-class instances (quantized int8) supporting ~150k steady tokens/sec total with headroom for session KV cache and average prefix lengths. This covers ~600 concurrent sessions with 35% active generating and average 220 token prefix.
- Peak/burst handling: Add autoscale burst pool (shared across tenants) capable of an additional ~300k tokens/sec to handle peak tails (longer responses). This is via dedicated burst capacity on A100 nodes and will fire based on queue depth/latency signals.
- Reranking batch: schedule on a separate batch pool overnight; 2 x batch-optimized GPU nodes will complete the 5k requests within the 2-hour window without impacting streaming pools.

Latency SLOs and routing:
- We can commit to p95 <= 120ms for interactive streaming on the Dedicated pool with the proposed sizing and placement (subject to final benchmark run with your dataset and prefix distribution). Achieving p50 50-70ms is feasible on A100-class variants; T4 will typically be slightly higher p50 but within your p95 target.

Next steps / asks from FinEx:
1) Confirm you are OK with the proposed dedicated/ burst split and whether procurement prefers firm capacity numbers for the MSA.
2) Share a small sample of typical prompts (sanitized) and representative request traces if possible for a final performance run (we'll run your prompts through our benchmark harness).
3) Confirm whether the mutual action plan document should include a DOCU/SIGN workflow or a manual signature route.

We will attach the cost estimate and a short performance-run plan in the next 48 hours. Rafael will include an explicit instance count + monthly estimate for both a Dedicated-only and Hybrid (Dedicated + burst) option.

If that sounds good, I'll schedule a 30-minute call for early next week to review the benchmarks and procurement items.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-sizing-calculator.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.docx
